children.text: The Philippines' signature resort island, famous for its roughly
4km
White Beach and paraw sailboat sunsets. It has grown even cleaner since a major environmental rehabilitation in
, and with direct flights from Korea to Kalibo, it remains a favourite for families and couples alike.
Boracay is a small island off the northwestern tip of Panay Island, part of the municipality of Malay in Aklan province, about
7km
long and less than
1km
wide at its narrowest point. On the island's west side, White Beach stretches for about
4km
of fine, flour-white coral sand, and at dusk, traditional paraw sailboats glide across a red sky, creating the scene travellers around the world remember in photos.

White Beach is divided into Stations 1, 2, and 3, named after the old boat landing points. Station 1 in the north has the widest sand and the most upscale resorts; Station 2 in the middle is the busy hub around D'Mall, packed with restaurants and bars; and Station 3 in the south is quieter, with more reasonably priced places to stay. On the island's east side, Bulabog Beach turns into one of Asia's best kitesurfing spots during the northeast monsoon season of
November–April
Boracay once suffered badly from overdevelopment and sewage problems, and the government closed the entire island to tourists for six months, from
April 26, 2018
to
October 25

, for a major rehabilitation. Since then, unlicensed structures along the beachfront have been torn down, drinking, smoking, and fireworks on the beach have been restricted, and a system requiring a confirmed accredited accommodation booking to enter the island has been put in place. As a result, today's White Beach is far cleaner and better organized than before.

With direct flights from Korea to Kalibo and many operators offering Korean-language service, Boracay is especially well suited to first-time visitors to the Philippines, families with children, and honeymooning couples. Its biggest draw is being able to enjoy everything from water activities to spas, fine dining, and nightlife on a single island.
Sail for about
1 hour
off White Beach at dusk aboard a traditional double-outrigger sailboat. A boat costs around
, and prices are negotiable.

blocks.title: Walk and swim at White Beach

children.text: Around
, Station 1 has the fewest people and the sand shines at its whitest. The gentle slope makes it great for swimming with children.
A half-day bangka tour covering Crystal Cove Island, Magic Island, a snorkeling spot, and Puka Shell Beach. A joiner tour costs about
per person.
A quiet beach at the island's northern tip, with more waves than White Beach and sand mixed with shell fragments. With fewer people around, it's a relaxed place to unwind.
The island's highest point at about
, offering a 360-degree view over all of Boracay and the surrounding sea. There's a small entrance fee.
During the northeast monsoon season of
November–April
, a row of kitesurfing schools opens for business. Beginner lessons typically run as multi-hour courses.
Try helmet diving, parasailing, an introductory scuba dive, jet skiing, and most other water sports here. Always book through an accredited operator.
A perennially popular half-day tour of cliff diving, snorkeling, and a beach barbecue on the coastal cliffs of Buruanga, on the mainland facing Boracay.

Check out, then leave from Cagban Port and head to the airport
It's about
1 hour
from Manila to Caticlan Airport (MPH, Godofredo P. Ramos Airport), with daily flights on Philippine Airlines, Cebu Pacific, and others. From the airport to Caticlan Jetty Port is about
5 minutes
by tricycle.
Kalibo International Airport (KLO) is an international airport with direct flights from Incheon, Busan, and other cities in Korea. From Kalibo to Caticlan Jetty Port takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
by bus or van, costing about
per person.
Flights to Caticlan and Kalibo are also available from Cebu.
From Caticlan Jetty Port to Boracay's Cagban Port takes about
15 minutes
by bangka, costing around
per person, plus separate terminal and environmental fees.
During the southwest monsoon season (
June–October
), boats sometimes dock at Tambisaan Port on the island's east side to avoid rough waves.
It's convenient to book a bundled transfer package covering airport pickup, the boat crossing, and island transport (about
per person).
The island entrance fee can be paid in advance through the online payment system (Boracay iPass). Check the latest notice.
Electric tricycles (e-trikes) are the main way to get around the island. A shared ride costs about
per person, and a charter costs about
depending on distance.
Along White Beach, it's most convenient to walk along the beachfront path behind the sand.
Boracay's seasons are shaped by the wind. From
November
to
May
is the northeast monsoon (Amihan) season, when White Beach on the island's west side is sheltered from the wind, giving it calm water and the clearest sea.
December–February
is cool and pleasant and the most popular time to visit, while March to
May
sees almost no rain but is the peak of summer heat, with midday temperatures climbing to around 34°C.
From
June
to
October

is the southwest monsoon (Habagat) season, bringing frequent rain, higher waves on White Beach, and more days with seaweed washing ashore. On the plus side, Bulabog Beach calms down and accommodation prices drop significantly. Flights and boats can be cancelled due to typhoons between July and
October
. In the third week of
January

, nearby Kalibo hosts the Ati-Atihan Festival, one of the Philippines' biggest celebrations. Rooms sell out early during Korean Lunar New Year and Chuseok holidays, as well as during Holy Week in the Philippines.

items.label: Accommodation
items.note: Only accredited accommodation may be used

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
In Boracay, only accommodations accredited by the Department of Tourism (DOT) may be used, and you'll be asked for proof of booking on arrival. Station 1 has upscale resorts from
a night and up; Station 2 offers mid-range hotels (
) with easy access to transport and restaurants; and Station 3 and the area behind the beach have more reasonably priced rooms in the
range. The large resort complexes on the island's north side are quiet, have private beaches, and are popular with families.

The food scene here is extremely varied. Buying shrimp, crab, and lobster at D'Talipapa market and having a nearby restaurant cook it for you — known as paluto — is a Boracay classic. Jonah's Fruit Shake's mango shake, a fixture since the

, and the calamansi muffin at Real Coffee & Tea Café have long been considered must-tries in Boracay. Several Korean restaurants are also on the island, so even picky family travellers have little to worry about.
Before arriving, prepare your accommodation booking confirmation (printed or on your phone) along with your passport. Entry can be delayed if your booking can't be confirmed.
There are several ATMs on the island, but they can run out of cash or have long lines during peak season, so bring some cash with you before you arrive.
The best spot to watch the sunset on White Beach is around Willy's Rock at Station 1. Stake out a spot before
Book water activities through your accommodation or an accredited operator rather than a beach tout, and always confirm exactly what's included in the price.
If your Kalibo flight arrives at night, check the boat schedule to Caticlan (service is limited overnight) and stay a night in Kalibo if needed.
During
November–April
, Bulabog Beach's strong winds make it better for watching kitesurfing than swimming — swim at White Beach instead.
If travelling with children, choose accommodation in a quieter section such as northern Station 1 or Station 3.
Smoking, drinking, littering, and building sandcastles are banned or restricted on White Beach, with fines for violations. Smoke only in designated areas.
Settle on a price up front for any activity, massage, or currency exchange offered by a beach tout, and avoid unlicensed operators. Exchange money at a bank or an authorized money changer.
Jellyfish appear at certain times of year, so check the beach safety flags and notices, and if stung, rinse with vinegar and seek medical attention.
Direct midday sun is very strong. Use reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral, and drink water frequently.
Environmental fees, terminal fees, and entry procedures can change under local government ordinances. Check the latest notice before you travel.
The whole island of Boracay operates under strict environmental rules. Keep in mind that "surely this is fine here" thinking can lead to a hefty fine.
